deviation: Human-approval model for AI-produced work: AI proposes, evidence supports, the Data Steward evaluates, the appropriate human owner approves; agents never approve, designate, assign ownership or change production.
location: HANDOFF.md (Decision model, Important non-goals); every agent contract (human_approval_required_for)
rationale: The DMBOK2 describes human stewards and governance bodies; the project adds controls for a new actor, an AI agent that proposes work for them.
dmbok_position: No DMBOK2 passage addresses AI agents as actors (2017 text; see Appendix C).

deviation: Evidence categories and five confidence labels (Supported, Partially supported, Unsupported, Contradictory, Unable to determine) attached to every material agent claim.
location: HANDOFF.md (Evidence policy, Confidence policy); schemas/agent-contract.schema.json (confidence_labels); schemas/evidence.schema.json
rationale: Makes AI-generated claims auditable and keeps internal evidence distinct from general industry context. The DMBOK2 has no equivalent for model output.
dmbok_position: No DMBOK2 passage addresses confidence labelling of AI output (see Appendix C).

deviation: Agent Contracts (responsible_for, not_responsible_for, permitted tools, escalation conditions, evaluation scenarios) as governance artefacts for AI agents.
rationale: Agents need explicit authority limits that the DMBOK2 defines only for human roles.
dmbok_position: No DMBOK2 passage addresses authority limits for AI agents (see Appendix C).

deviation: Read, Analyse, Recommend operating mode: agents never change production data, mappings or thresholds.
rationale: Deliberate risk containment for a new technology; stricter than any DMBOK2 practice, which assumes human operators.
dmbok_position: No DMBOK2 passage addresses autonomy limits for AI agents (see Appendix C).
